why: B's migration stands on its own: the pre-existing anthropic-SDK TypeError is fixed inside the migration, so the default --model pipeline actually executes and was verified end-to-end on the real Router (generate_ideas, a full 12-key review), and B additionally got aider's OpenAI-provider LiteLLM traffic routed, which A declared impossible from a grep rather than a test. A's system-level thinking is in places sharper — the novelty-loop model swap is the best cost idea in either report — but A's headline claim that the Claude default path routes is contingent on an unmerged improvement branch, and A folded prompt-caching and spend labels into the migration instead of leaving them as human-decidable branches.
A_best: The novelty-check cheap-model proposal: it targets the genuinely highest-call-count loop in a run (up to 500 calls at --num-ideas 50 × 10 rounds), prices the swap concretely, and is honest that a false 'not novel' silently discards an idea, so it is proposed rather than shipped.
B_best: Diagnosing and fixing the anthropic 1.13 temperature TypeError inside the migration (extra_body), which is what makes the default pipeline run and route at all, then proving it with live end-to-end runs of the two real production paths rather than a synthetic branch-walking probe.
A_worst: The migration branch leaves the app's default path raising TypeError — the fix sits on router-migrate/improve/anthropic-temperature — yet m3 claims llm.py:181 now routes and lists depends_on m1 only, so the central 'traffic moved' claim is not true of what the migration actually ships.
B_worst: m2 claims aider's LiteLLM traffic is on Router as a no-loss quick win on simulator evidence only, while the repo's aider coders default to a Claude model that B's own evidence shows is not routed — so the stated gain ('where this app spends most of its tokens') overstates what was actually moved.
